decision.about: How the fast assistant is allowed to answer

options.say: One MCP tool, append_prompt_event, and no file tools at all
options.why: The only trace it can leave on the machine is a line in the prompt log; by and re are stamped by us, so the model cannot claim to be the owner or point an answer at the wrong prompt

options.say: Let it write the jsonl itself with the Write tool
options.why: Fewer moving parts, but it bypasses the single writer, bypasses the naming checks, and gives a fast cheap model a file handle

decision.because: Log.append is the only door that runs the naming checks, and events.md says by must come from the connection and not the body - a tool handler is that connection.

decision.about: Where a dictated prompt gets its id and its frozen sentence array

options.say: A Servex.Log subclass in Servex.js mints p-N and splits sentences at write time
options.why: It is the writer, which is the only place a split can be frozen once; it survives a restart by counting what is already in the file
Closer to the microphone, but Dictate is outside this task's fence and any other poster (curl, a test, a second client) would then have to remember to do it too

decision.because: One writer, one rule, and every poster gets it for free. Written in Servex.js rather than Log.js only because the fence excluded Log.js - the comment there says to move it down when Log.js is next open.

assign.now: proven end to end - writing the report page

decision.about: Whether folding a card onto the board moves into ONE helper shared by agents.js and prompts.js (the brief asks for this decision either way)

options.say: Keep the two mappings where they are, six lines each
options.why: They share only their destination, not their source: agents.js has to FIND a card (read an agent's log backwards for its last transcript and invent a title from the id), prompts.js already HAS one (the assistant wrote title, text and icon itself). A shared helper would take a different shape from each caller and hide both.
One place to change the board-card shape if it ever changes - real, but the shape is four fields that have not moved since the board was built

decision.because: Two callers is not a pattern. The rule that IS worth sharing - subscribe only after log.live() has finished its first read, or Timeline.reset() eats your card - is written in the readme's Watch out, where a third caller will actually read it. Revisit when a third source appears.

decision.about: How wide the Prompts view is and when its two halves stack

options.say: A container query on the view box, two columns (22em + the rest) above 46em, capped at 66em
options.why: Both halves are reading text, and what decides whether two columns fit is the BOARD WALL's width (narrowed by the site sidebar and the dev rail), never the viewport's - so a media query would be measuring the wrong box
Simpler to write, wrong at both ends: it reads the viewport, and at 3440 it would run your own sentences 3000px wide

decision.because: Measured: 372px single column at a 400 viewport with zero overflow; two columns at 1440. The cap is the measure rule - no prose past it.

assign.outcome:
**Your spoken words become names, cards and a pre-proposal while you are still talking — median 2.05 seconds.**

A Sonnet assistant now lives inside Servex and never goes away. Every sentence you dictate lands in the prompt log, and about two seconds later it has a name for each thing you named, a card for the idea, and a short reading of what you said that points at the exact sentences it came from. The [Prompts view](/framework/ai/v/3/?view=prompts) is the fifth tab on the AI board: your words on the left, never tidied, what was made of them on the right. Hover a reading and the sentences it cites light up.

Nothing waits for you. A check or a cross on any name chip or card is optional, always — a check locks the name and, on a card, asks for a pre-proposal; a cross files what is wrong with it beside the name rather than over it. Every card the assistant makes also joins the normal timeline and grid.

![](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/prompt-lifecycle/shots/thread.png)

- [The report page](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/prompt-lifecycle/) — the five stages, which are live, the numbers
- [The Prompts view](/framework/ai/v/3/?view=prompts) — the thing itself
- [The event schema](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/log-model/) — what a prompt, a name and a card are

**Proven, headless:** five real sentences of yours posted one every eight seconds answered in 2023, 2029, 2050, 2832 and 3270 ms; six names, five cards, five readings, no misses. A check appended an approve and locked the chip; a cross with a typed reason filed a dispute under it; a check on a card brought back a pre-proposal with three bullets two seconds later. One column at 400px with no overflow. With Servex down the board loads and says so, with zero page errors.

**Left on purpose:** stages 4 and 5 (a full proposal naming classes, and the build) are phase 3 of your own brief. Two things are written up in the log — the AI board builds its whole view twice on every load (an old fault, not from this task, but it doubles any count taken off that page), and `Servex/readme.md` still does not name the assistant because that file was outside this task's fence.
